7984.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pleh₁- (“to fill”) and closely related to Latin plēbs, though the exact pre-form of the term is unclear.

7979.t: πλανάω (planáō, “to wander”) + -της (-tēs, masculine agent noun suffix)

7914.t: From Proto-Indo-European *pelito-, from *pel- (“gray”). Cognates include Sanskrit प॒लि॒त (palitá), Latin pallidus and Old Armenian ալիք (alikʻ, “wave; gray hair”).

7987.t: From πλησίον (plēsíon, “near”) + -άζω (-ắzō, “suffix for verbs”). Compare cognate πελάζω (pelázō) and old πιλνάω (pilnáō).

7919.t: From πέντε (pénte, “five”) + -άκις (-ắkĭs, suffix for adverb of repetition).

7971.t: From περι- (perĭ-, “beyond”) + -φρων (-phrōn, suffix for adjectives relating to the mind or emotions).

7994.t: An o-grade verbal noun from the root of πλέω (pléō, “to sail”) + -ος (-os).

7978.t: Probably from a Proto-Indo-European *peysd- (“to squeeze”), and cognate with Sanskrit पीडयति (pīḍáyati). The Indo-European root may be a d-extension of *peys- (“to grind, crush”), though such an enlargement is strange.

7925.t: Denominal verb from πέρα (péra, “beyond”); cognate with Albanian prura (“to bring, lead”).

7982.t: From πλέων (pléōn, “more”) + ἑκ- (hek-) (the root of ἔχω (ékhō, “to have”) + -της (-tēs).

7999.t: From ποίη (poíē), Epic/Ionic form of πόα (póa, “grass”), + -εις (-eis).

7986.t: From πλήρης (plḗrēs, “full, complete”) + φορέω (phoréō, “to bear, wear”).
